question.prompt:
Which cylinder has twice the volume of the cylinder shown at right?

[Figure 1](figures/1992_AMC_8_Q16_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
A cylinder's volume is its circular base area times its height:
\[
V=\pi r^2h,
\]
where \(r\) is the radius and \(h\) is the height. The original cylinder has radius \(10\) and height \(5\), so its volume is
\[
\pi(10)^2(5)=500\pi.
\]
We need a cylinder with volume \(2(500\pi)=1000\pi\).

Using the marked radii and heights, the choices have volumes
\[
\begin{aligned}
V_A&=\pi(20)^2(5)=2000\pi,\\
V_B&=\pi(10)^2(10)=1000\pi,\\
V_C&=\pi(5)^2(20)=500\pi,\\
V_D&=\pi(20)^2(10)=4000\pi.
\end{aligned}
\]
Only \(\boxed{\mathrm{B}}\) has twice the original volume.
